definitions.explanation: A gelatin-like substance made from red algae, used as a setting agent in Japanese cooking and confectionery. Unlike Western gelatin, it is plant-based and sets at room temperature. Widely used in traditional Japanese sweets (wagashi) and as a health food.

examples.japanese: {寒天|かんてん}でゼリーを{作|つく}った。
{寒天|かんてん}は{食物|しょくもつ}{繊維|せんい}が{豊富|ほうふ}だ。
examples.english: Agar is rich in dietary fiber.

examples.japanese: この{和菓子|わがし}には{寒天|かんてん}が{使|つか}われているので、{常温|じょうおん}でも{溶|と}けない。
examples.english: This Japanese sweet uses agar, so it doesn't melt at room temperature.

notes:
USAGE:
Unlike Western gelatin (ゼラチン), {寒天|かんてん} is plant-based (from seaweed) and sets firmly at room temperature. It is a staple ingredient in {和菓子|わがし} (Japanese confections) such as {羊羹|ようかん} and {水羊羹|みずようかん}. Also popular as a diet food because it is virtually calorie-free and high in fiber.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粉|こな}{寒天|かんてん}: powdered agar
- {棒|ぼう}{寒天|かんてん}: bar agar (dried stick form)
- {寒天|かんてん}ゼリー: agar jelly
- {寒天|かんてん}{寄|よ}せ: agar-set dish
